plan: This auction structure mirrors a second-price sealed-bid auction: the winner pays the second-highest bid (the clock price when the second-to-last bidder exits). In such mechanisms, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy - it maximizes expected profit regardless of others' bids. Bidding higher than value risks winning at a loss; bidding lower reduces win probability without improving price paid. Therefore, I will bid exactly my value of $26.

This auction functions like a second-price sealed-bid auction: the winner pays the second-highest bid, and my exit point is determined by my own bid. In such mechanisms, bidding my true value is the dominant strategy—it ensures I win whenever profitable (value > second-highest bid) and never overpay, since I only pay the lower competing bid if I win. Bidding above or below my value only risks losses or missed profitable wins. Therefore, I will bid exactly my value of $18.

This auction is effectively a second-price sealed-bid auction: I pay the second-highest bid if I win, regardless of my own bid (as long as mine is highest). The dominant strategy in second-price auctions is to bid my true value, as this maximizes expected profit without risk of overpaying or losing profitable opportunities. Bidding above value risks negative profit; bidding below risks losing profitable wins. Therefore, I will bid exactly my value of $21.
